assignment: Write a research lead's note on a proposed satisfaction claim and the next sampling plan.
source: Of 600 invited subscribers, 180 replied and 144 were satisfied. Of 400 invited former subscribers, 40 replied and 16 were satisfied. The team wants to advertise an 80% satisfaction rate for everyone ever invited. There are no known responses from nonrespondents. A small follow-up budget can support 50 short calls.

criteria.full: Computes respondent satisfaction of 80% in current and 40% in former subscribers, with response rates of 30% and 10%.
criteria.partial: Gets satisfaction percentages but omits differing response rates.

criteria.full: Explains why neither 80% nor the pooled respondent rate identifies satisfaction for all invitees.
criteria.partial: Mentions response bias without defining the claim's population.

criteria.full: Offers a transparent scenario or bound such as 16% to 94% overall with unrestricted nonrespondents, and states its assumption.
criteria.partial: Gives a weighted estimate as fact without a nonresponse assumption.

criteria.full: Allocates follow-up across the nonrespondent strata, prioritizes the underrepresented segment and defines how to report residual uncertainty.
criteria.partial: Suggests 50 convenient calls without a sampling frame.
